web_title: 5. Leading Operational KPIs, Structural Potential & CEO Walk-the-Talk
book_title: Chapter 5: The KPI Dashboard & Five-Year Management Accountability Audit
question: Are AvePoint's operational KPIs accelerating or maturing, and has CEO Tianyi Jiang delivered on his multi-year public-company promises?

epigraph.quote: FX-adjusted gross retention reached 90%—our target for several years—and net retention improved to 111%, while our $100K+ ARR cohort grew 28% year-over-year to 976 customers.
epigraph.author: James Caci, CFO, AvePoint Q3 2026 Earnings Call

web_blocks.html: AvePoint's operating scorecard through Q3 2026 shows steady execution at scale. Total ARR hit $495.1 million as of September 30, 2026 (+27% YoY reported; +25% FX-adjusted) [3, 4]. That marked the second straight quarter of faster FX-adjusted ARR growth, led by a record $30.0 million of net new ARR in Q3 (+34% YoY) [3, 4]. Remaining Performance Obligations (RPO) rose to $577.5 million at Q3 2026, up 21.5% YoY from $475.2 million [2]. About 60% of RPO (~$346.5 million) is set to book as revenue over the next 12 months, giving clear near-term visibility [2]. Upmarket enterprise wins are also accelerating [4, 5]. Customers paying >$100K ARR reached 976 in Q3 2026 (+28% YoY), with a record 65 net adds in the quarter [4, 5]. Cohorts above $250K, $500K, and $1M ARR each grew comfortably above 30% YoY [4, 5].

web_blocks.caption: AvePoint Multi-Year Operational KPI Trajectory (FY2021–Q3 2026)
web_blocks.takeaway: *Note: FY2022 ARR of $201.7M per FY2022 10-K (rebased to $214.7M in later presentations). Retention hit management's 90% GRR milestone in Q3 2026 despite a ~2-pt headwind from Fly migration.

web_blocks.html: Two Structural Watch Items in the KPIs: First, NRR (111% FX-adjusted in Q3 2026) sits below management's 115% medium-term goal [4, 5]. Cross-selling new SKUs like Control, AgentPulse, and Opus drives most expansion today rather than seat growth [4, 5]. CEO TJ Jiang noted on the Q3 2026 call that AvePoint prices AgentPulse by total employee count, not per-agent volume [4]. That keeps customer budgets predictable and eases adoption [4]. Yet it also exposes AvePoint to seat-count risk if AI agents shrink white-collar headcounts over the next decade [4]. Second, standalone AgentPulse revenue is still early [4]. AgentPulse customers grew >50% QoQ and managed agents >2x QoQ in Q3 2026, mostly via Control bundle upgrades [4]. Management expects meaningful standalone revenue impact in 2027 [4].

web_blocks.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
paragraphs: Management credibility is an underrated edge in small- and mid-cap software. In 2022, AvePoint promised 90% gross retention, a channel-majority book, Rule of 40, and GAAP operating profit. Skeptics pointed to its SPAC roots and 86% GRR. Four years later, the team has met all four operational promises. The next test is whether 2026's margin reinvestment sparks durable 2027–2029 AI-trust ARR acceleration.

book_paragraphs: When you and I check the operating dashboard through Q3 2026, the numbers show steady compounding execution. Total ARR reached 495.1 million dollars, up 27 percent reported and 25 percent FX-adjusted. That was the second straight quarter of faster growth, powered by a record 30 million dollars of net new ARR. Remaining performance obligations climbed to 577.5 million dollars, covering roughly 346 million dollars of revenue over the next year. Enterprise traction is also building: customers paying over 100,000 dollars a year jumped 28 percent to 976, with 65 added in Q3 alone.

Retention also hit a key milestone. For years, gross retention stayed in the high 80s—87 percent in 2022 and 2023, then 89 percent in 2024—dragged down two points by one-off Fly migration work. In Q3 2026, pooled customer success and better telemetry lifted FX-adjusted gross retention to management's 90 percent target. Net retention improved to 111 percent.

Now let's run an honest walk-the-talk audit on CEO TJ Jiang and CFO Jim Caci. Back in 2022 and 2023, they promised four milestones: 90 percent gross retention, GAAP operating profit, a channel-majority book, and Rule of 40 performance. By Q3 2026, they delivered all four. GRR stands at 90 percent, trailing 12-month GAAP operating margin is 10 percent, channel partners drive 60 percent of total ARR, and Rule of 40 sits at 44 percent.

Where are the gaps? First, non-Microsoft workloads still trail the long-term 30 percent goal, as Microsoft accounts for over 90 percent of ARR today. Second, NRR at 111 percent remains shy of the 115 percent target. AgentPulse is priced per employee rather than per AI agent, which lowers buying friction now but leaves seat-count risk if AI trims office headcounts later. Management reaffirmed its 2029 goal of 1 billion dollars in ARR and 27.5 percent operating margins—an ambitious bar, backed by a team that has earned trust.
